chunks: Aḥmad ibn Muḥammad ibn al-Ḥasan informed me, from his father, from Muḥammad ibn Yaḥyā and Aḥmad ibn Idrīs, from Muḥammad ibn Aḥmad ibn Yaḥyā, from Yaʿqūb ibn Yazīd, from ʿAbd al-Ḥamīd ibn Abī al-ʿAlāʾ or someone else, raising it, who said:

Al-Ḥasan ibn ʿAlī عليه السلام was asked: “What is the limit concerning relieving oneself?” He said: “Do not face the qiblah, and do not turn your back to it, and do not face the wind, and do not turn your back to it.”

Then he said, may Allah the Exalted support him: Urinating in still water is not permissible, and its mention has already passed. Then he said: There is no objection to it in flowing water, though avoiding it is better. And that which indicates this is:

key_terms.اجْتِنَابُهُ: avoiding it; refraining from the act as the preferable course
key_terms.الرِّيحَ: the wind, which should neither be faced nor have one’s back turned to it in this context
key_terms.الْغَائِطِ: relieving oneself; the act or place of defecation in legal context
key_terms.الْقِبْلَةَ: the direction of prayer that must be respected in bodily etiquette
key_terms.الْمَاءِ الرَّاكِدِ: still water, in which urinating is ruled impermissible here
key_terms.الْمَاءِ الْجَارِي: flowing water, in which doing so is stated to be unobjectionable though avoidance is better

ai.seo_question: What are the Islamic etiquette and rulings for relieving oneself according to Imam al-Ḥasan ibn ʿAlī عليه السلام?
ai.summary: This hadith gives legal etiquette regarding relieving oneself, including not facing or turning one’s back to the qiblah and avoiding exposure to the wind in that state. It also states the ruling against urinating in still water, while noting that doing so in flowing water is not objectionable though avoiding it is preferable.
